blocks.text: The limited standardized-format run started at 09:44:58 UTC on 26 October 2026. This post preserves the launch plan and early progress. Finished results are in a separate post.

Only the order of keys in training tool messages changes, to match the fixed runtime format. The earlier broader trial's settings, preserved 100-million-token base, fresh optimizer, seed, example order, tokenizer, 1,536-token context, and precision stay the same. All 3,000 conversations passed replay and token-limit checks. Assistant targets stayed unchanged, and no records were discarded.

The plan is exactly 499,839 assistant targets over 3,368 steps. Stopping between conversations leaves 161 targets unused below the 500,000 limit. A distinct pass still has 444,537 targets, so this repeats the same material rather than adding new data.

The trainer has a 3,600-second limit within a 3,780-second job limit. Saves are planned every 100,000 targets or 300 seconds. The separate project cutoff stays 31 October 2026 at 04:12 UTC. This run does not extend it.

Four evaluations on the two known development suites follow training. Old accepted-state scores stay separate from format, requested outcomes, and suggestion/date checks. The same 64 training IDs support a familiar-example fit check. No hidden final test is included.

At 09:46:23 UTC, the run had processed 162,906 targets at about 1,953 per second of process wall time and saved its first 100,000-target model. These are progress counts, not final fit or transfer results.

A corrected passive memory observer started during training after an earlier device-selection bug. Earlier maximum memory use remains unknown. Later whole-device samples cannot establish tensor-allocator peaks or measure work before observation began.

The idea is narrow: removing a known difference in input token order should make remaining fit failures easier to interpret. It does not predict reliable planning. This AI-assisted launch account was checked against launch records, matched budgets, settings, and the standardized-data record.
